ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 7312, as amended), Articles 5, 5-2, 5-3 and 20; Enforcement Decree of the Act, Articles 10, 11-2 and 15; Regulation on the Identification and Verification of Customers and Beneficial Owners issued by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU); Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 14370, as amended); and the Corporate Tax Act (Act No. 18521, as amended) for commercial registration, UBO identification, and substance requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate, Beop-in Deunggi-sawon)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Court Registry Office (Commercial Registration Division) under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarization (if requested by recipient) followed by apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA). Consular Legalization: for non-Apostille Convention destination states, the notarized document must be legalized exclusively by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that destination state; the apostille and consular legalization paths are parallel and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Registry Extract and Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Court Registry Office and the National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: official seals by the Korean National Tax Service and Court Registry are followed by a MOFA apostille. Non-Hague path: the same official documents undergo consular legalization through the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the destination state. Only one authentication path applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing formation, bank account opening, and inspection contracts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or initial members; notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public is followed by MOFA apostille for Hague member states; for non-member states, the notarized document is submitted to Korean consular authorities for consular legalization. No combination of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company founders and initial members; certified notarized copy by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague: notarized Articles of Association receive a MOFA apostille after the notary seal. Non-Hague: the notarized articles are legalized by Korean consular officials. The two authentication routes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a licensed Korean financial institution matching the target payment rails
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified Korean commercial bank holding the company preparatory or operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague states: bank authorized signatory plus MOFA apostille. For non-Hague states: bank authorized signatory plus Korean consular legalization. Neither path is chained with the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Unexpired Certificate of UBO and Signatory Identity and Address (notarized passport and proof of address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public for documents executed in Korea; Korean Embassy or Consulate abroad for overseas originals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued in Korea: notarized passport and address proof are apostilled by MOFA. If issued abroad in a Hague state: home-country apostille only; if issued in a non-Hague state: home-country consular legalization must be obtained prior to presentation in Korea. No cross-path chaining is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be conducted against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) designated lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance sanctions list, and Interpol Wanted Persons notices. A risk-based PEP identification process must cover all politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, with enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, source-of-wealth verification, ongoing transaction monitoring, and periodic rescreening at least annually under FATF Recommendations 10, 12, and 24. All screening must be automated with manual analyst review and documented for audit trails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (i-REGIS) of the Supreme Court of Korea - Company Registration Search and Name Clearance (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in Korean Hangul script using a phonetically accurate transliteration of any foreign name. The limited liability suffix Yuhan Hoesa must be included in the registered name. The four-tier naming convention consists of the proprietary identifier, the business purpose description, the liability indicator (Yuhan Hoesa), and the legal form class. If an English trade name is desired, it may be recorded as a separate romanized alias only after the Hangul name is cleared and must be shown in parentheses in all official filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must submit a written request for correction and re-examination to the registry office within 14 days, citing Article 23 of the Korean Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act. If the re-examination is denied, an immediate appeal may be filed to the High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, with the court required to rule without unnecessary delay. Separately, an administrative revocation lawsuit may be filed in the Administrative Court within 90 days of the rejection notice. The applicant may request a stay of the registration deadline during appeal and may engage a certified judicial scrivener or attorney to expedite the process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is legally permissible in Korea only if it corresponds to an actual serviced address with mail handling, telephone reception, a local corporate secretary, and a valid lease that satisfies the National Tax Service for business registration. For the on-site factory pre-shipment inspection and quality control industry, pure virtual office arrangements are rejected by Korean tax authorities and banks because the entity must demonstrate operational capacity, physical inspection equipment, personnel presence, and local audit substance. A business registration number will be denied or cancelled if the registered office is found to be a mere mailbox with no supporting lease, utilities, payroll, or physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist includes: (1) signboard and interior signage; (2) premises lease registered under the company name; (3) utility bills and internet subscription in the company name; (4) payroll or retainer records of at least one local representative; (5) normal office operating hours; (6) fire safety and building management logs; (7) inspection equipment or transportation assets. Quantified risk: unannounced on-site visits by municipal tax office or National Tax Service field investigators are likely at a moderate 30-40% occurrence within the first fiscal year for new registrations, rising to 60% if no employees are declared, if the office is a residential conversion unit, or if the registered address is a virtual-only mailbox. An adverse inspection can lead to cancellation of the corporate registration and adverse immigration consequences for foreign directors.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean Commercial Law Attorney or Certified Judicial Scrivener formation and registration fee (drafting Articles of Association, board minutes, and UBO affidavit)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean licensed attorney or certified judicial scrivener
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa formations, inclusive of English/Korean drafting and filing, USD 700-1,200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean Court Registry registration and license tax for LLC incorporation (registration tax, education surtax, and court application fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Court Registry Office and local municipal government
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Registration and License Tax Act; approximately 0.2% of declared capital plus 20% education surtax, subject to minimum, plus fixed court application fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association and Power of Attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Fee Rules under the Act on Notarial Acts, fixed notarial tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: MOFA apostille or consular legalization of documentary bundle (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA) or Korean consulate abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular Fee Act and MOFA administrative fee schedule; approximately USD 5-10 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office serviced office with physical presence and mail handling for one year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office provider or landlord in Seoul business district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for serviced office with physical workstations, mail handling, and telephone reception, USD 80-120 per month plus deposits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and issuance of Company Registration Record
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official court convenience fee set by the Court Administrative Office, approximately KRW 1,000-3,000 converted at 1,300 KRW/USD.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening database licenses and source-of-wealth file preparation for up to three beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party compliance data providers and KoFIU-registered screening bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard for low-risk AML/CFT screening of a single legal entity and up to three beneficial owners for one year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 288-330 (Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa), Article 543 (Board of Directors), Article 393 (Authority of Directors), and Article 397 (Duty of Loyalty); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) Articles 2, 5, and 6 for foreign-invested entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (법원등기국) via the Korean Court Registration Information System (인터넷등기소), with local jurisdiction at the Seoul Central District Court Registry (서울중앙지방법원 등기과) for the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Certificate of Incorporation Registration Application (법인설립등기신청서), filed under the Commercial Act and the Registration of Real Estate and Other Rights Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). However, the initial capital must be fully paid in at the time of incorporation, and the paid-in amount must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company (or a designated escrow account) until the registration is completed. The deposit certificate must be submitted to the registry. For foreign investors, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires a minimum foreign investment of KRW 100 million (approximately USD 75,000) to qualify for FIPA incentives, but this is not a statutory incorporation requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) — ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 368(4) OF THE KOREAN COMMERCIAL ACT. 

WHEREAS, the undersigned, being the sole director and sole shareholder of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), a limited liability company duly organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, desires to take certain actions to effectuate the initial corporate governance and operational setup of the Company; 

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED, as follows: 

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: That the Company has received full and lawful subscription for its entire authorized share capital of KRW 100,000,000 (One Hundred Million Korean Won) divided into 100,000 ordinary shares of KRW 1,000 par value each, and that such shares are hereby allotted to the sole shareholder, [Name of Shareholder], in consideration for the full cash payment deposited into the Company's designated bank account at [Bank Name], Account Number [Account Number], as evidenced by the deposit certificate attached hereto. The Board confirms that the paid-in capital is fully paid and free of any encumbrance. 

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the Company shall open and maintain corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and any other financial institution as the Director may deem necessary. The Director is hereby authorized to execute all account opening documents, signatory cards, and any related agreements. The Director shall have sole signatory authority for all transactions, provided that any transaction exceeding KRW 50,000,000 shall require the prior written approval of the shareholder. 

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Full Address, including building name, floor, and unit number], Seoul, Republic of Korea. The Director is authorized to execute a lease agreement for such premises, to file all necessary notices with the Korean Court Registry, and to take all steps to maintain the registered office in good standing. 

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That the following officers are hereby appointed to serve in the capacities indicated, each to hold office until resignation or removal by the Board: (a) [Name] as Director and Chief Executive Officer, responsible for overall management and legal representation of the Company; (b) [Name] as Auditor (Gamsa), who shall be independent and not an employee of the Company, to supervise the Company's financial affairs and compliance with the Commercial Act; and (c) [Name] as Company Secretary, responsible for maintaining statutory records, minutes, and filings. Each officer shall execute an acceptance of office and shall comply with all fiduciary duties under Korean law. 

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: That the Director and officers are hereby authorized to execute, deliver, and file all documents, pay all fees, and take all actions necessary to effectuate the incorporation registration, obtain business licenses, and commence operations, including but not limited to the issuance of corporate seals, tax registration, and any other regulatory filings. 

6. EFFECTIVE DATE: This resolution shall be effective immediately upon adoption. 

ADOPTED this [Day] day of [Month], [Year], by the sole director and shareholder, in accordance with the Company's Articles of Incorporation and the Korean Commercial Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Pre-incorporation Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Court Registration Information System (인터넷등기소) and any commercial bank in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the online registry portal (or in person at the local court registry) to ensure the proposed company name 'Yuhan Hoesa' is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered entities. Simultaneously, open a temporary capital deposit account at a Korean commercial bank in the name of the future company (or the incorporator's name) and deposit the full initial capital (e.g., KRW 100,000,000). Obtain a certificate of deposit (예금잔액증명서) from the bank, which must be dated within 30 days of the incorporation registration. The name reservation is valid for 6 months. Ensure the name includes the suffix '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) as required by law.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of the incorporator
Power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, file an appeal with the registry or select an alternative name. If the deposit certificate is expired, obtain a new one from the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and the Korean Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in Korean, including mandatory provisions: company name, purpose (technical testing and analysis services under ISIC 7120), registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, capital amount, method of public notice, and appointment of initial directors and auditor. The Articles must be signed by all incorporators (or their legal representatives) and notarized by a Korean notary public. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the notarization is mandatory. After notarization, the Articles become the foundational document for registration. Ensure the business purpose clause explicitly covers 'commercial inspection, testing, and quality control services' to align with the ISIC code and future licensing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, revise the Articles and re-notarize. If the registry later queries the purpose clause, file an amendment resolution and re-register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation Registration with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry) via online or in-person filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application (법인설립등기신청) to the competent court registry within 14 days of notarization. The application must include the notarized Articles, the capital deposit certificate, the list of directors and auditor, their written acceptance of office, and the registered office lease agreement or consent of the property owner. Pay the registration fee (approximately KRW 300,000, including court fees and local taxes). The registry will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the registry issues a Certificate of Registration (등기사항증명서) and assigns a corporate registration number. This step legally creates the company as a separate legal entity.
required_dossiers: Acceptance of office forms from directors and auditor
Lease agreement or consent for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order (보정명령), rectify the specified deficiencies within the given period (usually 2 weeks). If the application is rejected, file a new application after curing the defects. If the registration is delayed, request expedited review with justification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Business License Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) and Local Municipal Office (구청)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, register for corporate tax and business operations with the National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax system (홈택스). Obtain a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) by submitting the incorporation certificate, Articles, and lease agreement. Additionally, register with the local municipal office for local taxes (e.g., business place tax). For the specific business of commercial inspection and testing, apply for any industry-specific licenses (see licensing section). Also open a corporate bank account in the company's name using the business registration certificate. Finally, register for the four major social insurance schemes (national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, industrial accident insurance) with the respective authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the business purpose, provide the Articles and explain the scope. If the local office requires additional permits, obtain them before finalizing the business registration. If the bank account opening is delayed, use a temporary account for capital deposit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korean Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS) under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), and the Korea Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (KOLAS) under KATS
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Testing and Inspection Agency Registration (시험검사기관 등록) under the Framework Act on the Management of Quality of Industrial Products and the Act on the Promotion of Development of Testing and Inspection Technologies

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (환경부) and local Environmental Management Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – The business is a service-based inspection and testing agency with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or waste generation. However, if the agency operates a laboratory with chemical reagents, it may require an Environmental Registration (환경등록) under the Chemicals Control Act and a Waste Disposal Agreement. For pure on-site factory inspections without a fixed laboratory, EIA is Not Applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If a laboratory is operated: wastewater discharge must comply with the Water Quality Conservation Act (COD ≤ 40 mg/L, BOD ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 40 mg/L for standard discharge); volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions must be below 100 ppm per stack under the Clean Air Conservation Act; hazardous waste must be handled by a licensed waste contractor and disposed of within 180 days. If no laboratory, these standards are Not Applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (소방안전증명) from the National Fire Agency (소방청) for the registered office and any laboratory premises, including compliance with the Fire Safety Standards for Buildings (e.g., fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation plans). Occupational Safety and Health Administration (KOSHA) approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including a workplace safety inspection and a written safety management plan if the company employs 5 or more workers. For on-site factory inspections, a Certificate of Liability Insurance for professional indemnity may be required by clients.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, e-filing portal: HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For Yuhan Hoesa, a Korean resident limited liability company established by foreign investors: (1) register the legal entity with the Korean Commercial Act at the local court registry, thereby obtaining a corporate registration certificate; (2) register the local place of business with the competent district tax office; (3) submit the business commencement ('business registration') application to the tax office, which issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN); this BRN is used as the corporate TIN and VAT identification code. Foreign non-resident shareholders are required to report the foreign investment to Invest Korea and provide notarised identification documents; a domestic tax representative is advisable for service of tax notices if the foreign shareholder has no Korean resident agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for passthrough/check-the-box. Korean corporate income tax is applied at entity level. Separate group 'consolidated corporate tax filing' election is available under Article 76-4 of the Corporate Tax Act for a resident parent corporation and its 100% owned resident subsidiaries, subject to related deadline and approval conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – Korean VAT Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 80,000,000 in annual taxable revenue (approximately USD 60,000); voluntary registration is allowed below this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all B2B transactions. Every electronic tax invoice must be issued and transmitted to the HomeTax system in real-time via the authorised NTS API or e-invoice service provider. The invoice includes a National Tax Invoice number and an electronic signature; no separate anti-fraud stamp or fiscal clearance by the tax authority is required, but submission is monitored in real time for mismatch detection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act and its enforcement decree, zero-rating applies to exported goods and exports of certain services provided to non-residents, including cross-border quality-control and inspection services where the service is physically performed in Korea but the recipient is situated abroad and the consideration is paid in foreign currency. The exporter/importer must prove that the goods or services were actually supplied outside Korea or for a non-resident, the foreign payment was received, and all customs/export formalities were completed. For services to a foreign customer, a written contract and invoice showing the services are provided to a non-resident are typically required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic export declaration (export bill of entry / export declaration number)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing international carriage
Foreign exchange receipt certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank (equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate / FIRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger a reassessment of unpaid VAT plus a statutory additional tax: 10% of the wrongfully credited zero-rated tax for mere reporting defects; 20%-40% for negligence/fraud (approach depending on the seriousness). The NTS may also seek criminal sanctions for VAT evasion and impose a collection surcharge where repayment periods exceed 180 days. Claims must be supported by the export declaration, payment evidence and foreign exchange receipts; otherwise the zero-rating is clawed back retrospectively with penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberal but documentary-heavy foreign exchange regime. Current account receipts and payments in ordinary trade and services are freely convertible through licensed foreign exchange banks; no prior MOEF approval is normally required, although each remittance must be supported by the underlying contract or invoice and must be reported through the bank FETA platform. Capital account items, including foreign direct investment, intercompany loans, and acquisition of foreign securities, are also convertible but require filing or review with MOEF and BOK through the designated bank, especially when the amount exceeds regulatory thresholds or the foreign investment exceeds KRW 100 million. The system does not impose forced surrender of foreign exchange for resident manufacturing or quality-control businesses. There are no recurring KRW conversion quotas; exporters may retain foreign currency in onshore foreign currency deposit accounts. The main friction is documentary rather than convertibility: profit and dividend remittance requires the Korean LLC to have paid withholding tax and filed national tax clearance, and capital repatriation must be traced to the original FDI report. In practice, BOK does not act as a day-to-day censor for valid inspection, testing, and quality-control service payments when the underlying trade evidence is clear.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and its delegated regulations, export proceeds for services and pre-shipment inspection or quality-control contracts must be collected within 180 calendar days after the service completion date or the contractual settlement date, unless the responsible foreign exchange bank grants an extension. The mandatory conversion ratio to KRW is 0 percent for ordinary exporters; there is no standing requirement to sell foreign exchange earned from inspection services to the central bank or a licensed bank. The exporter may retain the proceeds in a designated foreign currency deposit account with a Korean foreign exchange bank. The bank requires underlying service contracts, inspection reports, invoices, and a receipt confirmation. If an invoice is settled in KRW, the bank applies the market exchange rate and records the transaction under FETA reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. Fintech EMIs such as Wise are not licensed in Korea as foreign exchange banks under FETA and cannot open the type of corporate FDI capital account, report capital transactions to Korean regulators, or perform withholding tax settlement required for a Yuhan Hoesa. They may be used for low-value ancillary payments through bank-sponsored payment services, but the statutory corporate account and all equity injection must remain at a domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence of the statutory representative or a Korean-resident attorney-in-fact is generally mandatory for initial corporate account opening. Most Tier-1 banks do not permit fully remote consular proxy opening for a newly formed LLC. The statutory director must authenticate identity via passport, and if a power of attorney is used, it must be in Korean, notarized at the Korean consulate or apostilled, and the attorney-in-fact must appear in person with original corporate documents. A video KYC interview with the ultimate beneficial owner is also standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The LLC is newly formed with non-resident ultimate ownership and the bank cannot yet confirm the underlying commercial substance of the planned pre-shipment inspection and quality-control agency operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and corporate registration excerpt, Korean business licence, Articles of Association, ISO/IEC 17020 or equivalent inspection-body accreditation where applicable, detailed operating plan, office lease, utility invoice, staff roster, and three projected customer contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an offshore parent triggers source-of-funds review; third-party remittance or a large lump-sum equity creation may be flagged as potential money laundering or undisclosed external borrowing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized board resolution authorizing the capital contribution, audited or reviewed financial statements of the investor for the last two years, banking reference from the remitting bank, six months of bank statements showing traceable funds in the investor own account, source-of-wealth questionnaire, and an FDI receipt report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank sees payment flows to or from jurisdictions associated with manufacturing clients, especially China, Vietnam, or other high-volume trade countries, raising sanctions and trade-based money-laundering concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete customer and end-client identification list with beneficial owners, signed service contracts, inspection reports with site and date evidence, customs and shipping documentation, transaction-level invoices, sanctions and OFAC screening report, and AML/KYC questionnaires for all high-risk counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction volume is inconsistent with the low-value inspection and quality-control fee model; multiple remittances from unrelated parties would collide against the company stated operational account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated cash-flow projection and historical transaction ledger, contract reconciliation package matching each fee collection to a specific factory inspection report, tax invoices issued under Korean VAT law, no-cash and no-crypto certification, and monthly management accounts reviewed by the licensed accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions from the foreign shareholder should be remitted from the shareholder own corporate account to the LLC designated foreign currency or KRW account at a Tier-1 commercial bank using SWIFT MT103. The bank application must quote the foreign exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment or foreign equity contribution. A copy of the foreign investment report, corporate registration certificate, board resolution, and certificate that no minimum capital is due should be provided. The receiving bank will issue a foreign exchange receipt certificate, and the reporting to the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency or the foreign exchange bank should be completed if the investment meets the FIPA threshold. Funds should be held as capital, reconciled to the FDI report, and not commingled with operational receipts before capital verification is recorded.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating payments, use SWIFT MT103 for standard cross-border service disbursements below USD 500,000; use a confirmed or unconfirmed Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 for capital machinery, sampling equipment, and large audit or pre-shipment supervision commitments; use documentary collections for repeated medium-value trade flows with established suppliers. Each disbursement must be submitted to the Korean bank with the underlying contract and tax invoice, the applicable FETA payment purpose code, and a statement on whether withholding tax has been satisfied. The bank will screen counterparties, verify the goods and service description, and file the outward remittance report. Never split a single transaction to avoid review thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank against USD/KRW and other convertible currencies with a clear trade payable or receivable exposure and no leverage.
FX swap contracts for matching the timing of foreign currency tax payments, dividend remittances, or trade settlement obligations.
Plain vanilla FX options purchased from a Tier-1 bank, with premiums paid from operational funds and exercised only with confirmed underlying exposure.
Cross-currency swaps arranged through the same foreign exchange bank to hedge a registered intercompany loan or FDI capital balance, with MOEF and BOK reporting if applicable.

Boundary: offshore non-deliverable forwards and speculative synthetic KRW products are not permissible as a primary hedging rail for a resident Korean operating entity without documented underlying exposure and prior bank approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of members with adoption of financial statements and auditor appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ under the Korean Commercial Act; meeting minutes and adopted financial statements must be retained at the registered office and produced on demand to the National Tax Service or district court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual general meeting is not itself an administrative strike-off event, but the adopted financial statements may be invalid, directors may face civil liability to members, and repeated non-cooperation with tax or registry requests can lead to court-imposed fines or forced closure after formal correction orders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system, when the company is subject to external audit; a copy must also be delivered to shareholders and stored at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31, subject to a court-approved extension not exceeding 45 days where audit delay is justified
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing of the external audit report may result in administrative fines up to KRW 50 million, criminal fines up to KRW 30 million, and imprisonment up to three years under the Act on External Audit of Accounting Firms; persistent violation can trigger supervisory sanctions and court-ordered liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return together with attached financial statements and tax reconciliation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via the HomeTax system at the competent local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers statutory surcharges of 20% of the unpaid tax if paid after the statutory deadline and 30% if paid more than six months after the deadline, plus 0.022% daily interest; prolonged non-filing allows the tax office to seize assets, commence collection proceedings, and petition for judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surcharge return on the corporate income tax liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government through the National Tax Service HomeTax collection channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as the corporate income tax return, which is within three months after fiscal year-end and by March 31 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The local surcharge is assessed at 10% of national corporate income tax; non-payment attracts the same local surcharge penalties and collection procedures as the national corporate tax, including mandatory delinquency surcharges and property seizure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Second-period value-added tax return and annualized VAT reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the second VAT period covers July 1 through December 31 and is filed by January 25 of the following year; the first VAT period covers January 1 through June 30 and is filed by July 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT returns attract a penalty of 10% of the unpaid VAT plus daily interest of 0.022%; false or missing electronic tax invoices can create additional penalties up to 2% of the supply value, and repeated non-filing may result in business registration closure and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment report for non-resident shareholding or share-transfer events
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency in coordination with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any foreign investor acquires shares, changes ownership percentage, or increases the foreign investment amount beyond the approval threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a foreign investment report can result in administrative fines up to KRW 5 million and loss of statutory protections for dividend and liquidation remittance, but does not alone dissolve the company; repeated non-compliance with foreign exchange reporting can be referred to criminal enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual surveillance assessment for the commercial inspection and testing statutory accreditation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Laboratory Accreditation Scheme administered by the Korean Agency for Technology and Standards under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual surveillance assessment before each anniversary date of the accreditation certificate; the core accreditation cycle is three to five years but the annual surveillance is mandatory in each intervening year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missed surveillance assessment results in suspension or withdrawal of KOLAS accreditation; conducting commercial inspection or quality-control testing without valid accreditation may attract administrative fines under the Industrial Standardization Act up to KRW 30 million and a corrective closure order, and inspection reports lose legal evidentiary weight

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit, minute-book update, and corporate records reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company management; records are subject to production on demand by the district court company registry, National Tax Service, and anti-money-laundering compliance examiners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the annual general meeting date each year; a full reconcilement of the register of members, director changes, registered address, and share-transfer records must be completed before the filing of the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient or falsified statutory registers can jeopardize directors limited-liability protection, impede share transfers, and create evidentiary disadvantages in litigation; failure to maintain a required registered office allows the court to declare the company dormant and proceed with administrative cancellation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Accounting Firms, a Yuhan Hoesa must obtain an independent certified CPA audit when any of the following conditions is met: (i) the entity is a listed company or a securities issuer registered with the Financial Services Commission; (ii) total assets at the end of the preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9 million; (iii) the entity is a financial company, investment company, collective investment scheme, or other regulated entity designated by Presidential Decree regardless of asset size; (iv) the entity voluntarily elects to be audited under its articles of incorporation or by member resolution. There is no standalone revenue or employee-headcount trigger that creates an audit obligation for a non-regulated private Yuhan Hoesa; revenue and headcount are nevertheless used by the Presidential Decree to determine SME classification and to decide whether the simplified audit procedures are available. Forced audit can also be ordered by the court or tax authority if statutory records are unreliable or public interest requires an independent examination.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards are mandatory for companies subject to statutory external audit, listed companies, and entities electing to use K-IFRS. Non-public small and medium Yuhan Hoesa companies that do not meet the external audit threshold may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles as promulgated by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, including the SME Accounting Standards. Financial statements must be expressed in Korean won and must be integrated with the settlement of accounts adopted at the annual general meeting of members.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO confirmation filing for private limited liability companies. Instead, the Yuhan Hoesa must keep accurate beneficial-ownership information available for banking partners, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, and the National Tax Service on request. Any transfer of membership units must be recorded in the register of members without delay, and a transfer of a share interest is ineffective against the company until the transferee is entered in that register. For foreign investors, an acquisition or transfer of an ownership interest equal to or exceeding the Foreign Investment Promotion Act threshold must be reported within 30 days. At least annually, when relationships with regulated financial institutions are revalidated, the company must reconfirm its ultimate beneficial owner and report any mismatch through the relevant customer-due-diligence channel.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages over company assets
Minute Book containing general meeting and written resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 3,000 per year for professional corporate secretarial, registered-office, and compliance-agent services in Seoul or Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 to USD 22,000 per year for a certified CPA audit of a small-to-mid-size Korean Yuhan Hoesa with total assets between KRW 12 billion and KRW 100 billion; USD 3,000 to USD 7,000 for a voluntary review-level accountant report if external audit is not mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.5% (progressive national CIT rates 10%,20%,22% and 25%, plus 10% local income tax surcharge)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays, Free Economic Zone and Free Trade Zone income tax reductions, Special Tax Treatment Control Law R&D and job-creation credits, patent box/IP royalty exclusion, and international shipping or export support regimes

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 5 (Corporate Tax Base and Amount of Tax Statement) filed via the National Tax Service Hometax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with semi-annual provisional corporate tax payments in April and October for corporations with previous-year tax liability)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the return is due by March 31 of the following year, and a one-month extension may be granted for overseas branch operations or certain foreign-controlled taxpayers upon pre-application

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate operating revenue from on-site factory inspection, pre-shipment testing, quality certification and audit agency services including invoices issued to foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source inspection revenue unless the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a permanent establishment of a foreign principal; in that case, the foreign principal should report the attributable profit on the same return and attach the Foreign Corporation Domestic Business Place statement; cross-border service revenue must be cross-checked against the TP documentation file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, subcontract fees, wages, rent, depreciation, consumed materials and statutory provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees, quality-control technology fees and group service charges are deductible only if arm's length, actually rendered and beneficial to the Korean entity; the NTS may disallow any fee that duplicates economic functions, is booked without a service agreement, or is not supported by time allocation, cost records and CIGA evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after permanent and temporary book-tax adjustments, non-taxable income, exemptions, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation without a Korean PE must not file a business profit return at all; a PE taxpayer must allocate only profit attributable to the domestic business and claim treaty business-profit protection only where no PE threshold is breached; do not combine exempt offshore receipts in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the progressive national corporate income tax bracket rates before local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-controlled Korean entity, national tax is computed at the same graduated rates as a resident entity; the local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of CIT is then imposed and combined in the total corporate tax payable; tax credits and prior year advance payments must be reconciled with the provisional payment slips.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 14e - Foreign Tax Credit and Withholding Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign taxes paid on income also taxable in Korea and reconciliation of Korean taxes withheld from interest, royalty or dividend remittances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa is treated as a Korean resident on an election or PE basis, it may claim direct foreign tax credits using the underlying foreign corporation schedule; if it is simply the Korean payer of outbound profits, use the non-resident withholding remittance form and DTA relief form instead of this box, and do not add treaty-reduced taxes into the CIT credit unless a resident branch is present.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Supplementary Schedule - Non-Resident Ownership and Foreign Transaction Particulars
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual declaration of the ultimate beneficial owner, foreign shareholder register, and details of every cross-border related-party transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every foreign related party, provide the legal and beneficial ownership chain, state the country of residence, and mark every transaction type that exceeds KRW 5 billion; failure to attach the TRC and beneficial ownership declaration in this schedule will trigger refusal of treaty WHT relief and AML review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax (40% for fraudulent omission), daily overdue surcharges at the statutory statutory-added rate currently around 0.025% per day on underpaid tax, penalty tax of up to KRW 5 million for failure to file foreign transaction particulars, and criminal punishment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act of up to five years imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 100 million for deliberate evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge, producing a combined effective rate of 22% on outbound dividends paid to a non-resident corporation unless reduced by an applicable bilateral tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home jurisdiction, deliver it to the Korean withholding agent before the payment date, complete the Application for Non-Resident Income Tax Exemption or Reduction (Form 120-1), evidence beneficial ownership of the dividend, describe the economic substance and CIGA of the Korean payer, provide board resolutions, ownership charts and dividend flow statements, and file through the NTS Hometax DTA module; if any element is missing, the Korean payer must withhold the 22% domestic aggregate rate and the refund route is administratively available but subject to the same substantiation before appeal.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is also 20% national withholding plus 2% local surtax, aggregate 22%; treaty rates generally reduce interest to 5%-15% and royalties to 5%-10%, and in some DTA clauses technology/copyright royalties are exempt, but the same TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, IP creation/substance map and actual payment proof are required before treaty treatment is applied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion per foreign related-party transaction type for mandatory Local File preparation and KRW 10 billion of aggregate related-party transactions or KRW 100 billion of revenue for mandatory Master File preparation; country-by-country reporting attachs when the Korean group generates consolidated revenue equal to or above KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not legislate a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the tax administration applies substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, Principal Purpose Test and Core Income-Generating Activities analysis through the International Tax Adjustment Act and tax treaties; the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must operate actual inspection and quality control functions through its own employees, premises, equipment, contracts and revenue-bearing activities, and the actual directors must control the core business decisions, otherwise the entity may be re-characterised as a conduit or shell for treaty and anti-avoidance purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa books fictitious pre-shipment inspection invoices, inflates intercompany management fees, or understates Korean-source QC revenue in the annual CIT return to shift profits to a zero-tax foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraudulent understatement attracts an additional tax of 40% of the evaded tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes and, on referral, criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act of imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to KRW 100 million; confiscation of the evaded corporate assets is authorized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The National Tax Service pierces the corporate veil, assesses the directors personally for the evaded corporate tax and local surtax, files civil restitution claims for stripped assets, imposes a travel ban/blacklist on directors residing in Korea, and a court conviction disqualifies the director under the Commercial Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Korean entity as a letter-box company without premises, staffing, bank activity or CIGA exclusively to route dividends and royalties through South Korea and claim a reduced bilateral treaty withholding rate for an ultimate shareholder in a third state.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority denies treaty relief under the Principal Purpose Test and applies the domestic 22% withholding plus accuracy penalties; the Corporate Tax Act and International Tax Adjustment Act allow upward tax adjustment for the full deemed under-withholding and recharacterize the intermediary entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are held jointly and severally liable for the entire tax deficiency under the veil-piercing doctrine; the NTS issues a departure ban and asset seizure order, and directors face criminal exposure for aiding a fraudulent tax claim where they knowingly execute the sham structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity uses nominee shareholders, fails to identify the true non-resident controller in the foreign transaction report, or remits dividends without filing the DTA-related beneficial ownership declaration to avoid a Financial Intelligence Unit alert.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-disclosure of beneficial ownership in cross-border payments violates the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Financial Transactions Reports Act, carrying fines up to KRW 100 million and an additional tax levy for undisclosed income, with referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit for money-laundering assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal oversight exposes directors to asset freeze, FIU blacklisting, departure restrictions, disqualification from corporate governance roles, and imprisonment of up to five years for concealment of criminal proceeds or aiding money laundering; personal assets are attachable when the corporate treasury has been depleted.
